newsitem.title: UK: LME ALUMINIUM CORRECTS LOWER IN LATE TRADING.
newsitem.headline: LME ALUMINIUM CORRECTS LOWER IN LATE TRADING.

text.p: Aluminium corrected lower in late inter-office trading on Thursday as players took profits after a squeeze boosted prices above forecasts.

Three months aluminium rallied to $1,775 per tonne, the highest since early last October, but then drifted lower to be indicated at $1,755/58 at 1800 GMT after a kerb close of $1,762.50, up $21 on the day.
Copper meandered around the kerb close of $2,333, initially slipping but then recovering ground to be indicated at $2,326/29.
Earlier it broke above resistance at $2,320, which sparked some short-covering to push the metal to a high of $2,335.
Other LME metals were broadly unchanged to slightly weaker.
